query: Mowing Day {Today the enchanted scythes are mowing the Flight Field, swinging themselves in neat lines while the groundskeeper sleeps under a tree.|Mowing day. A game has sprung up among the scythes: run the line without breaking stride. The groundskeeper is asleep again.|The scythes are out. You know their rhythm now: swish, step, swish, a pause on every seventh.} {The smell of cut grass is everywhere.|Somebody's hat has already been mown in half.|{season == "summer": Heat shimmers over the stubble.|A light drizzle makes the grass shine.}} Run the scythe line {You dart through the line and out the other side without a scratch. The watching first-years make you do it again.|Swish, step, swish. You run the whole line and arrive at the end breathless and laughing.|You run the line on the seventh-beat pause and it feels like dancing. Nobody else has timed it that well.} {A scythe catches your robe and neatly removes a sleeve. You trip on the stump of it. The groundskeeper wakes, looks, and goes back to sleep.|You trip on a tussock and fall flat as the scythes pass politely overhead. The first-years cheer, the wrong way.|You mistime the seventh beat and go sprawling. Your hat joins the other hat. Your pride follows.} Rake hay for the stables {You rake the cut grass into rows for the stables. The groundskeeper wakes long enough to give you a coin and a nod. Your palms blister.|You rake until the field is striped and your arms are lead. The stables send a crown, and a hippogriff's thanks.|You rake with the scythes' rhythm in your arms. The groundskeeper pays you without waking, which is a skill in itself.}
